title: Stage 2: graceful shutdown with a deadline
summary: Stop accepting, drain what is queued, cancel what overruns the deadline, and let a stopping signal finish the job in hand.

steps.title: The brief
body: Deploys happen ten times a day. Each one stops the pipeline, and today that loses or half-runs jobs. Two kinds of stop:
- **`StopAsync(drainTimeout)`**, called by the host on SIGTERM: stop accepting new jobs, let the workers finish what is queued,
but if that takes longer than `drainTimeout`, **cancel the token the handlers were given** and return once they have stopped.
A job cancelled this way counts as `Failed` (its message would be retried by the broker in a real system).
- **The `stopping` token passed to `Start`**: workers stop **taking** jobs but **finish the one in hand**. So handlers must no
longer receive `stopping`; they get a separate token that only the drain deadline cancels.

steps.prompt: During shutdown, which token should each thing listen to?
buckets: the drain-deadline token (abort work in progress)
items: the worker's wait for the next job
the handler's HTTP call to the partner
the decision to read one more job from the channel

steps.prompt: Why can the worker loop no longer use `await foreach (var job in reader.ReadAllAsync(stopping))`?
options: When `stopping` is cancelled it throws out of the loop, so the worker task faults and `StopAsync` sees an exception
It reads two jobs at a time
steps.explain: Use `WaitToReadAsync(stopping)` + `TryRead`, check `stopping` before taking each job, and treat the cancellation as a normal end of the loop.

steps.title: Stop cleanly
prompt: 1. `StopAsync(drainTimeout)`: stop accepting (`TryEnqueueAsync` returns `false` from now on), complete the channel, wait for the
workers; if they are not done within `drainTimeout`, cancel the handlers' token, then wait for the workers to end. It never throws
2. Handlers receive a token cancelled **only** by the drain deadline (not by `stopping`).
3. When `stopping` is cancelled, each worker finishes its current job and takes no new one.
4. A handler cancelled by the deadline counts as `Failed`.
Everything from stage 1 must keep working.

template: var p = new Pipeline(new PipelineOptions(4, 3, TimeSpan.FromSeconds(2)), async (job, ct) =>
for (var i = 0; i < 12; i++) await p.TryEnqueueAsync(new Job($"j{i}", "t1", i == 5 ? "boom" : "ok"), CancellationToken.None);
Dojo.Check("No jobs accepted after StopAsync", !await p.TryEnqueueAsync(new Job("late", "t1", "ok"), CancellationToken.None), "TryEnqueueAsync should return false once stopping began.");
await Dojo.TryAsync("The drain deadline cancels a job that overruns", async () =>
var p = new Pipeline(new PipelineOptions(4, 1, TimeSpan.FromSeconds(2)), async (job, ct) =>
var returned = await Task.WhenAny(stop, Task.Delay(3000)) == stop;
Dojo.Check("StopAsync returns soon after the deadline", returned, "StopAsync was still waiting 3 seconds later: cancel the handlers' token when drainTimeout passes.");
Dojo.Check("The handler saw the cancellation", sawCancel, "Pass the handler a token that the drain deadline cancels.");
Dojo.Eq("The cut-off job counts as failed", 1, p.Failed);
await Dojo.TryAsync("The stopping token finishes the job in hand and takes no more", async () =>
var p = new Pipeline(new PipelineOptions(4, 1, TimeSpan.FromSeconds(2)), async (job, ct) =>
if (job.Id == "j1") { handlerToken = ct; inFirst.TrySetResult(); await gate.Task; }
foreach (var id in new[] { "j1", "j2", "j3" }) await p.TryEnqueueAsync(new Job(id, "t1", "x"), CancellationToken.None);
Dojo.Check("The handler's token is not the stopping token", !handlerToken.IsCancellationRequested, "Handlers should only be cancelled by the drain deadline.");
Dojo.Eq("Only the job in hand ran", "j1", string.Join(",", ran));
hints: Add a `CancellationTokenSource _abort` and give handlers `_abort.Token`. In `StopAsync`, `Task.WhenAny(all, Task.Delay(drainTimeout))`; if the delay wins, `_abort.Cancel()`, then `await all`.

Replace `ReadAllAsync(stopping)` with `while (await reader.WaitToReadAsync(stopping)) while (!stopping.IsCancellationRequested && reader.TryRead(out var job)) ...`, inside `try { } catch (OperationCanceledException) when (stopping.IsCancellationRequested) { }`.
An `int _accepting = 1` flag set to 0 at the top of `StopAsync` lets `TryEnqueueAsync` refuse at once.
explain: Plug this into a host with a `BackgroundService` whose `ExecuteAsync` calls `Start(stoppingToken)` and whose `StopAsync` calls
`pipeline.StopAsync(...)` with a drain timeout a few seconds shorter than `HostOptions.ShutdownTimeout`, which in turn is shorter than
the pod's grace period. Then a deploy never cuts a job in half without knowing it.
